text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Iraq and Russia sign deal to develop one of Iraq's largest oilfields; Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Rodionov says implementation will start regardless of U.N. trade sanctions.
- Explosion hits Tel Aviv.
- More food flows into country after oil-for-food deal.
- Washington concerned about security of its troops in Gulf.
- Deputy Prime Minister Aziz continues meetings in Brussels.
- Justice Minister Maliki in Islamabad for Islamic conference.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article says Iran's holding of Iraqi POWs is against teaching of Islam.
- Industry and Minerals Ministry ferries more industrial goods to markets.
- More tourist projects in Shi'ite holy city of Najaf.
IRAQ
- Police catch gang accused of murdering several citizens and stealing number of cars.
JUMHOURIYA
- Japan signs deal to buy Iraqi crude oil.
- United Nations allows Libyan pilgrims to use Egyptian planes for pilgrimage to Mecca.
- Editorial criticises United States for hypocritical attitudes.
- Week of solidarity with Iraqi POWs in Iran starts on Saturday.
- Article on Israeli lobby in current U.S. administration.
